newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA OWES 2.569 BLN MARKS TO IMF, INTL LENDERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA OWES 2.569 BLN MARKS TO IMF, INTL LENDERS.

text.p: Bulgaria owed the lev equivalent of 2.569 billion marks to the IMF and other financial insititions on July 31, a month after Bulgaria introduced a currency board system, central bank figures showed on Monday.
Under the currency board, a form of an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate regime, the lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark as anchor in the system from July 1.

Debt to the IMF stood at the mark equivalent of 1.490 trillion levs while liabilities to other international financial institutions amounted to 1.079 trillion levs on July 31. Liabilities also included other debts of 7.8 billion levs.
The debts are entered as liabilities in the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) Banking Department monthly balance sheet.
Total Banking Department assets and liabilities, including equity amounted to 3.560 trillion levs at end-July, balance sheet figures showed.
The BNB capital, a part of the Banking Department liabilities comprised 20 billion levs own capital, 698.3 billion levs of reserves and 265.7 billion of retained profit on July 31.
The department's assets included government debt of 1.194 trillion levs. Bulgaria's IMF quota and holdings in other international financial instititions totalled 1.087 trillion levs.
Prior to the introduction of the currency board the BNB separated its balance sheet between the Banking Department and the Issue Department, which manages the country's foreign exchange reserves.
The Banking Department deposit with the Issue Department, part of the Banking Department's assets and a liability of the Issue Department totalled 792.0 billion levs on July 31.
The Banking Department assets also included 293.3 billion levs of investments in sucurities and 74.2 billion levs of non-monetary gold and other precious metals.

Refinancing to banks less provisions, which is also a part of the Banking Department's assets amounted to 17.9 billion levs. Equity investments in domestic entities totalled 2.1 billion levs at end-July.
The Banking Department, a lender of last resort for local commercial banks under the currency board, can refinance sound banks only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system.
